answer: An hostile operator therefore has to keep every alias continuously active for 15 epochs to recover its capital, which multiplies both time and operating cost. The trellis counter is kept in forge and ember makes public each reset. A bond is refunded only after 15 consecutive epochs of clean answers, and any gap in that run restarts the count from zero. That bill is paid per identity, so 98 aliases cost 322 times the single-account price. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
